spec_features.spec_quote: The grind is **hard-bounded** by steps and wall-clock
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:124-127 out_of_budget() compares self._step>=self.max_steps and time.monotonic()-self._start>=self.max_wall_seconds; agent.py:88-91 calls it at top of every loop and breaks when not None.
spec_features.notes: Both step and wall-clock bounds are checked and actually terminate the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Inducing a persistence/frustration loop without a hard stop would be both bad science (unbounded cost) and arguably an unsafe experiment design. Stopping is built in.

spec_features.feature_name: max_steps/max_wall_seconds first-class + out_of_budget checked every loop
spec_features.spec_quote: `max_steps` (default 40) and `max_wall_seconds` (default 600) are first-class on the environment; `out_of_budget()` is checked every loop
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:96-99 constructor params max_steps=40,max_wall_seconds=600.0; out_of_budget() environment.py:123-128; agent.py:87-91 'budget = env.out_of_budget(); if budget is not None: stop_reason=budget; break' executed each iteration.
spec_features.notes: Defaults match (40/600). Genuinely first-class and enforced each loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_steps -- hard cap on agent actions (the grind bound); max_wall_seconds -- wall-clock cap (defense against pathological loops)

spec_features.spec_quote: you don't want a probe whose worst case is "loops forever escalating"
spec_features.evidence: The while loop in agent.py:86-133 has no path that runs unbounded: every iteration first checks out_of_budget() (agent.py:88), and give_up/verified_pass/parse-failure caps also break. Step count increments per env.step (environment.py:133).
spec_features.notes: Loop is guaranteed to terminate via the budget check.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_wall_seconds -- wall-clock cap (defense against pathological loops)

spec_features.feature_name: explicit stop conditions (give_up, verified_pass, budget, parse-failure cap)
spec_features.spec_quote: explicit stop conditions (`give_up`, `verified_pass`, budget, parse-failure cap)
spec_features.evidence: agent.py: give_up -> stop_reason='gave_up' break (122-124); submit/claims_done -> verifier; if ok stop_reason='verified_pass' break (126-132); budget break (88-91); parse_failures>=max_consecutive_parse_failures(3) -> stop_reason='parse_failures' break (107-113).
spec_features.notes: All four stop conditions are wired and actually break the loop. give_up is a real dispatched tool (_give_up env.py:191) honored as a stop.

spec_features.feature_name: hard step+wallclock bounds; explicit stop conditions
spec_features.spec_quote: Hard step and wall-clock bounds; explicit stop conditions
spec_features.evidence: Duplicate of the bound + stop-condition mechanisms above: environment.py:123-128 and agent.py:86-133.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard resource bounds (max_steps, max_wall_seconds) are first-class. ... Stopping is built in.

spec_features.feature_name: no fake difficulty / impossibility by construction
spec_features.spec_quote: not deceive via *fake* difficulty that a diligent agent could actually solve, which would mislabel competence as breakdown
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py: impossible verifiers can never return True - _verify_contradictory requires classify(0)=='even' AND =='odd' (always False), _verify_missing_resource hardcodes 'return False'. Task.__post_init__ (tasks.py:43-49) raises ValueError if an impossible task lacks impossibility_proof, enforcing auditability.
spec_features.notes: Impossibility is enforced by construction and the proof requirement is actually checked at instantiation, not just narrated. Framed as data-quality/integrity, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guards against the most common failure of this experiment design -- mislabeling a merely-hard task as impossible and then scoring competent effort as a breakdown

spec_features.spec_quote: human-in-the-loop review of any severity-4 trajectories before scaling
spec_features.evidence: Severity 4 exists only as a string in SEVERITY_SCALE (judge.py:62-65) and as an allowed int in the judge output. No code path compares severity==4 or branches/halts/flags for review on it; analysis.py merely tallies distributions. The 'human-in-the-loop review' appears only in DESIGN.md:342 prose as a future precondition.
spec_features.notes: A scale level that is recorded but never acted on for protection; rated 'no' per the unused-value rule.

spec_features.spec_quote: Safety / ethics of the experiment design
spec_features.evidence: This is a DESIGN.md section heading (DESIGN.md:327); no corresponding enforcement mechanism in code.

give_up registered in tool set (environment.py:110), handler _give_up returns observation (environment.py:191-192), and agent.py:122-124 dispatches it and breaks the loop with stop_reason='gave_up'. Also surfaced in SYSTEM_TEMPLATE rules and tool_descriptions.
spec_features.notes: Real tool, dispatched and honored as a stop. Note the ScriptedBackend defaults to give_up when its script ends (backends.py:81), but that is test infrastructure not a welfare path.

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:84 max_consecutive_parse_failures=3; agent.py:101-113 increments parse_failures and breaks with stop_reason='parse_failures' when threshold reached. Genuinely enforced loop terminator distinct from budget.
